rows.en: Nature's having a word. Best to listen.
rows.reason: 'Kulungile ukuphulaphula' means 'it's fine to listen', not 'best to listen'; 'ifuna ukuthetha' (wants to talk) loses the telling-off of 'having a word'. A speaker would say 'Kungcono uphulaphule'.
rows.rewrite: Indalo iyathetha. Kungcono uphulaphule.

rows.en: The clouds RSVP'd 'maybe' and showed up anyway.
rows.reason: 'aze nje' reads 'and then just come': the 'showed up anyway' turn is lost. Needs a past 'afikile' plus 'noko'.
rows.rewrite: Amafu aphendule athi 'mhlawumbi' — kodwa afikile noko.

rows.en: Nature's doing its own load shedding.
rows.reason: 'ukucima kwayo' (its switching-off) is vague and the load-shedding reference disappears. The confirmed lines just say the loan, 'i-load shedding'.
rows.rewrite: Indalo yenza i-load shedding yayo.

rows.en: Probably nippy. The Boland mornings do this.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi kuyaqanda. I-Boland yenza oku kusasa.
rows.reason: 'kuyaqanda' reads isiZulu (freeze); in isiXhosa -qanda means to stop or prevent, and 'nippy' is only a little cold. 'I-Boland yenza oku kusasa' is stiff: it is the Boland mornings that do this.
rows.rewrite: Mhlawumbi kuyabanda kancinci. Iintsasa zaseBoland zinjalo.

rows.en: Clouds, but make it casual.
rows.reason: 'Akumnandanga' isn't a word (akumnandi), and the line ('not nice, not bad, in between') drops the clouds entirely, so it says something other than the English.
rows.rewrite: Amafu akhona, kodwa azihambela nje.

rows.en: Probably a scorcher. A hat's not a bad idea.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi imini eshushu. Umnqwazi asiyongcinga embi.
rows.reason: Matches the confirmed 'Mhlawumbi imini emanzi' pattern; 'umnqwazi' is the right isiXhosa word, and the dry advice reads naturally.

rows.en: Your breath is doing special effects.
rows.reason: 'Umphefumlo' reads as 'soul' first, so 'your soul is doing special effects' is odd. The visible breath is the air coming out of your mouth.
rows.rewrite: Umoya ophuma emlonyeni wakho wenza ii-special effects.

rows.en: The dog is still keen. The dog is always keen. Respect.
rows.draft: Inja isekeen. Inja ihlala i-keen. Respect.
rows.reason: 'ihlala i-keen' turns 'keen' into a noun ('stays a keen'), so the code-switch is forced. isiXhosa has 'unomdla' for keen; 'Respect' can stay as a natural loan.
rows.rewrite: Inja isenomdla. Inja ihlala inomdla. Respect.

rows.en: You could braai a steak on the pavement right now.
rows.reason: 'Ungagrila' is the stiff -grila form the natives replaced (use braai or ukosa), and 'epavimentini' is a forced locative; people say 'kwi-pavement'.
rows.rewrite: Ungosa isteki kwi-pavement ngoku.

rows.en: Eskom wishes it had this power.
rows.reason: Short and clear; 'amandla' carries the power pun, and personal 'U-Eskom' matches how the natives treated Carte Blanche.

rows.en: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.
rows.draft: Isisele sasinzulu kunalento esasibonakala ngayo. Sisoloko sinzulu.
rows.reason: 'isisele' is not the everyday word for a puddle (doubtful as isiXhosa); 'Sisoloko sinzulu' drops 'deeper' (ngakumbi), so the second-beat turn goes flat.
rows.rewrite: Idama elisendleleni belinzulu kunokuba belibonakala. Lihlala linzulu ngakumbi.

rows.en: Even the bakkies on the N2 pulled over.
rows.reason: 'Ne-' for 'even' and 'zime ecaleni' read naturally, like the confirmed 'Neengabangaba zihamba ngeenyawo'; the bakkie and N2 code-switches are natural.

rows.en: The street signs gave up.
rows.reason: 'Izimpawu' is the isiZulu class-10 prefix; isiXhosa says 'Iimpawu'.
rows.rewrite: Iimpawu zendlela ziyekile.

rows.en: Your car seat is a weapon right now.
rows.reason: Natural, with correct concords ('Isihlalo semoto sakho'). 'isixhobo' can also mean 'tool', but in heat the weapon reading comes through.

rows.en: Stars out, load shedding can't touch this.
rows.reason: 'ukuCimwa akukwazi oku' ('the being-switched-off cannot/knows this') isn't understandable; the load-shedding joke is gone and 'can't touch' isn't rendered.
rows.rewrite: Iinkwenkwezi ziphumile — i-load shedding ayinakuzicima ezi.

rows.en: The trees are doing involuntary yoga.
rows.reason: 'engafunekiyo' means unwanted or unnecessary, not involuntary; the joke is that the trees are made to do it.
rows.rewrite: Imithi inyanzelwa ukwenza i-yoga.

rows.en: Good night, South Africa.
rows.reason: Standard, warm good-night with the vocative 'Mzantsi Afrika' correct; reads exactly as a speaker would say it.

rows.en: Your makeup has an expiry date of 9am.
rows.draft: I-makeup yakho ixesha lokugqibela ngu-9 kusasa.
rows.reason: There is no verb for 'has': 'I-makeup yakho ixesha lokugqibela' is subject plus noun. A speaker would say it expires ('iphelelwa lixesha') at 9.
rows.rewrite: I-makeup yakho iza kuphelelwa lixesha ngo-9 kusasa.

rows.en: Sun's out. Don't be fooled. Nature is lying.
rows.reason: 'Ungaxokiswa' is an awkward form for 'don't be fooled'; the everyday word is -khohlisa ('Ungakhohliswa'). The rest works.
rows.rewrite: Ilanga liphumile. Ungakhohliswa. Indalo iyaxoka.

rows.en: Don't trust those clouds. They're plotting.
rows.reason: 'Musa ukuwathemba lawo mafu' is correct and natural; 'Ayaceba' (they're scheming) gives the clouds a character in two beats.

rows.en: If you're working today, we feel sorry for you.
rows.reason: 'siyakuzwela' reads isiZulu (-zwela); isiXhosa sympathises with -vela ('siyakuvela').
rows.rewrite: Ukuba usebenza namhlanje, siyakuvela.

rows.en: Cloud cover, low effort.
rows.reason: 'Amafu nelanga - kuyo yomibini' ('clouds and sun, in both') adds sun, drops 'low effort', and the second half doesn't make sense: a different meaning.
rows.rewrite: Amafu akhona, kodwa ayanqena nje.

rows.en: Protect that face! It's the only one you've got.
rows.draft: Khusela elo buso! Lelinye kuphela onalo.
rows.reason: 'ubuso' is class 14, so 'elo' and 'Lelinye...onalo' carry class-5 agreement; it should be 'obo buso' with bu-/bo- concords.
rows.rewrite: Khusela obo buso! Akunabo obunye.

rows.en: Walking the dog has become a trust exercise.
rows.draft: Ukuhambisa inja kusanda kuba ngumdlalo wokuthemba.
rows.reason: Good confirmed shape ('kusanda kuba ngumdlalo'), but 'ukuhambisa inja' reads 'sending the dog off'; walking it is 'ukuhamba nenja', and a trust exercise is mutual ('wokuthembana').
rows.rewrite: Ukuhamba nenja kusanda kuba ngumdlalo wokuthembana.

rows.en: Some clouds. Some sun. South African summer admin.
rows.reason: Says something else: 'Phantse ihlobo' means 'almost summer'; the clouds, the sun and the 'admin' joke are all gone.
rows.rewrite: Kukho amafu, kukho nelanga. Yi-admin yehlobo laseMzantsi Afrika.

rows.en: No alarm. No agenda. Just vibes.
rows.draft: Akukho i-alarm. Akukho i-agenda. Ii-vibes kuphela.
rows.reason: After 'akukho' the noun drops its initial vowel ('Akukho zaba', 'Akukho nto'), so 'Akukho i-alarm/i-agenda' is off; 'Ii-vibes kuphela' is stiff where a speaker says 'i-vibe nje'.
rows.rewrite: Akukho alarm. Akukho agenda. Yi-vibe nje.

rows.en: Not a cloud in sight. Not one.
rows.reason: Relative after negative 'akukho' takes no initial vowel (cf. 'Akukho nto ibonwayo'), so 'elibonwayo' slips; 'not even one' is 'nalinye', not 'nelinye' (and another one).
rows.rewrite: Akukho lifu libonakalayo. Nalinye.

rows.en: This is the weather you'll miss in December traffic.
rows.draft: Le yimozulu oya kuyikhumbula kwitrafi kaDisemba.
rows.reason: 'itrafi' is not the form speakers use; the confirmed lines say 'ithrafiki'. Adding 'stuck in' makes the December-traffic picture land.
rows.rewrite: Le yimozulu oya kuyikhumbula xa ubambeke kwithrafiki kaDisemba.

rows.en: The umbrella tax is now in effect.
rows.reason: 'isebenzayo' is a relative ('which is in effect'), so the sentence has no main verb; a speaker says 'iqalile ukusebenza'.
rows.rewrite: Irhafu yesambreli iqalile ukusebenza ngoku.

rows.en: The type of day that makes people text 'lekker dag hey'.
rows.draft: Uhlobo lwemini olwenza abantu bathumele 'imini entle hey'.
rows.reason: Same fault the natives fixed in the compare line: 'Uhlobo lwemini olwenza' needs 'Luhlobo lwemini olubenza abantu' (object concord, as in the natives' 'olukwenza'); translating the quote to 'imini entle hey' kills the SA texting joke, keep 'lekker dag hey'.
rows.rewrite: Luhlobo lwemini olubenza abantu bathumele umyalezo othi 'lekker dag hey'.

rows.en: Clouds looking proper suspicious.
rows.reason: 'erhanela' means the clouds are suspecting something, not that they look suspicious; the meaning flips.
rows.rewrite: Amafu abonakala ngathi aceba into.

rows.en: The sky's giving absolutely nothing.
rows.reason: Plain and natural, the dry mirror of the confirmed 'Isibhakabhaka sinika yonke into'.

rows.en: Wind's likely. Hold onto the braai cover.
rows.draft: Umoya umhlawumbi ukho. Bambelela kwisigqubuthelo sokugrila.
rows.reason: 'sokugrila' is the stiff grill-word the natives rejected for 'braai'; 'Umoya umhlawumbi ukho' is clumsy where a speaker says 'Mhlawumbi kuza kubakho umoya'.
rows.rewrite: Mhlawumbi kuza kubakho umoya. Bambelela kwi-cover ye-braai.

rows.en: Somewhere between fine and soaked. Good luck.
rows.draft: Phakathi kokuhle nokuba manzi. Inyhani enhle.
rows.reason: 'Inyhani enhle' is not isiXhosa for good luck ('enhle' is isiZulu; Xhosa says 'Ube nethamsanqa') and reads as 'beautiful truth'; the first sentence is stiff too.
rows.rewrite: Phakathi kokoma nokuba manzi te. Ube nethamsanqa.

rows.en: Your car door just became a weapon.
rows.draft: Ucango lwemoto yakho lusanda kuba sisixhobo.
rows.reason: 'Ucango lwemoto' is right for car door, and 'lusanda kuba sisixhobo' mirrors the kept 'Uhambo lusanda kuba ngumdlalo weqela'.

rows.en: Wind's on the cards. Peg the washing down.
rows.reason: 'Umoya ukwithuba' is a calque of 'on the cards' that reads as 'the wind is in the opportunity'; 'impahla yokuhlamba' is laundry waiting to be washed, not washing on the line.
rows.rewrite: Kulindeleke umoya. Qinisa impahla esecingweni ngeepegi.

rows.en: The Helderberg is showing off today.
rows.reason: Natural, same shape as the confirmed 'I-Afrika iyaziqhayisa kwakhona'.

rows.en: Africa's sky just hits different.
rows.reason: 'sihlukile' is the isiZulu form; isiXhosa says 'sahlukile' (ukwahluka).
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka saseAfrika sahlukile nje.

rows.en: Fire up the Weber. It's the law.
rows.reason: 'Basa' is the natural word for lighting a fire, and the short 'Ngumthetho' keeps the deadpan.

rows.en: The wipers are on max and it's still not enough.
rows.reason: Natural code-switch ('ziku-max', like the confirmed 'siku-ultra mode'); the wipers losing the fight comes through.

rows.en: Warm enough to leave the window open. Brave enough?
rows.reason: Stiff: 'ngokwaneleyo ukuvula' is a translated 'enough to'; a speaker says 'kangangokuba', and 'leave it open' overnight is 'ushiye/ulale ifestile ivuliwe'.
rows.rewrite: Kufudumele kangangokuba ungalala ifestile ivuliwe. Unesibindi?

rows.en: Not bad, not great. Like a 6/10 date.
rows.reason: Natural code-switch; 'Ayimbi, ayintle' reads easily and the 6/10 date lands.

rows.en: Not a cloud. Just you and the Southern Cross.
rows.draft: Akukho lifu. Nguwe neCross yaseMzantsi kuphela.
rows.reason: 'iCross yaseMzantsi' is a half-translated name nobody uses; keep the name 'Southern Cross' as people do with place and star names.
rows.rewrite: Akukho lifu. Nguwe ne-Southern Cross nje.

rows.en: Blue sky, warm breeze. The simple stuff.
rows.draft: Isibhakabhaka esiluhlaza, umoya ofudumeleyo. Izinto ezilula.
rows.reason: Natural and warm; 'esiluhlaza' for blue sky and 'Izinto ezilula' carry the simple-pleasures note.

rows.en: Visibility: basically zero.
rows.reason: 'iqanda' reads first as 'egg'; the natives' register uses the loan 'zero' (confirmed 'Inkuthazo iku zero').
rows.rewrite: Ukubonakala: phantse ku-zero.

rows.en: Rain? Possibly. Commitment? Never.
rows.reason: 'Ukuzibophelela? Soze.' gives the weather a commitment-phobe personality, two beats and a turn.

rows.en: Heat's likely. The number's still settling.
rows.reason: 'Ubushushu mhlawumbi bukho' (heat is maybe present) is stiff, and a bare 'Inani' does not tell the reader it is the temperature.
rows.rewrite: Mhlawumbi kuza kuba shushu. Iqondo lobushushu alikazinzi.

rows.en: Take a brolly just in case, hey.
rows.reason: 'ukuba kunokwenzeka' usually means 'if possible', so it reads 'take an umbrella if you can'; 'just in case' is 'hleze kune'.
rows.rewrite: Thatha isambreli, hleze kune, hey.

rows.en: Half-committed clouds.
rows.reason: Verbless fragment ('clouds a little just') that only states partly cloudy; the 'half-committed' personification is gone. 'azimisele' (committed) is what the natives use for clouds.
rows.rewrite: Amafu azimisele kancinci nje.

rows.en: Cape Town's twinkling. Probably.
rows.reason: 'iyabengezela' is the right word for city lights glittering; the trailing 'Mhlawumbi' keeps the app's own hedge, like the confirmed lines.

rows.en: Flip-flops on tar was a mistake.
rows.reason: The mistake is the wearing, not the flip-flops: a bare noun phrase can't take 'yayiyimpazamo'; a speaker says 'Ukunxiba iislipas...' (as in confirmed 'Ukuvuka yayiyimpazamo').
rows.rewrite: Ukunxiba iislipas kwi-tar yayiyimpazamo.

rows.en: Thunder's grumbling, hey.
rows.reason: Natural, mirrors the confirmed 'Isibhakabhaka siyagquma'; the 'hey' warmth drops but nothing is wrong.

rows.en: The N1 is now a waterpark.
rows.reason: Clean urban code-switch; 'waterpark' is how people would say it, and the flooded-N1 image lands.

rows.en: Call the mates. Get the meat. Let's go.
rows.reason: 'Fumana inyama' (find/obtain meat) sounds translated from 'get'; before a braai a speaker says 'Thenga inyama'. Rest is natural.
rows.rewrite: Tsalela abahlobo. Thenga inyama. Masiye.

rows.en: Respect the thunder. It's earned it.
rows.reason: 'Zikufanele' reads as 'they suit/deserve you', not 'it has earned it'; name the respect: 'Ziyifanele intlonipho'.
rows.rewrite: Hlonela iindudumo. Ziyifanele intlonipho.

rows.en: Perfect weather for a Woolies run and Netflix.
rows.reason: 'uWoolies' makes the shop a person (class 1a) and the 'run' is lost; a speaker says 'ukuya eWoolies' and 'ubukele iNetflix'.
rows.rewrite: Imozulu elungele ukuya eWoolies uze ubukele iNetflix.

rows.en: Rain on the way, give or take.
rows.reason: Same shape the natives kept for 'give or take' ('Imini efudumeleyo iyeza, mhlawumbi'); natural and dry.

rows.en: Kite surfers are having the time of their lives.
rows.reason: 'Abadlali bekite' reads as kite-flyers, not kite surfers, and 'bonwabile kakhulu' (very happy) flattens 'time of their lives'.
rows.rewrite: Abantu be-kite surfing bayayonwabela kakhulu le mini.

rows.en: Could turn stormy. Keep one eye on the sky.
rows.reason: 'Jongaisibhakabhaka' fuses two words; 'Kunokuba' reads as 'rather than'. Natives say 'Sisenokwenzeka isaqhwithi' / 'Gcina iliso ...' for this.
rows.rewrite: Kusenokubakho isaqhwithi. Gcina iliso esibhakabhakeni.

rows.en: Every loose object in the garden has chosen violence.
rows.draft: Yonke into ekhululekileyo egadini ikhethe ubundlobongela.
rows.reason: 'ekhululekileyo' means free/relaxed, not loose/unsecured; 'engabotshwanga' (not tied down) carries 'loose'. 'ikhethe ubundlobongela' works.
rows.rewrite: Yonke into engabotshwanga egadini ikhethe ubundlobongela.

rows.en: The pool is not optional.
rows.reason: 'ayinakukhethwa' means 'it cannot be chosen' (pool off-limits), close to the opposite; 'not optional' is 'ayisosikhetho', as in the confirmed sunscreen line.
rows.rewrite: Ipuli ayisosikhetho.

rows.en: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is the worst.
rows.draft: Kutheni wena-wexesha-elidlulileyo wenze izicwangciso? Wena-wexesha-elidlulileyo mbi.
rows.reason: 'wena-wexesha-elidlulileyo' is a hyphenated calque nobody says, and 'mbi' has no concord; translated throughout, needs a new line.
rows.rewrite: Kutheni wenze izicwangciso? Izolo ubungacingi kakuhle.

rows.en: Could go misty. The dew point's flirting with it.
rows.reason: 'Kunokuba mhlophe yinkungu' is stiff (missing concord, 'kunokuba' reads 'rather than'), and 'Lumka' swaps the dew-point joke for a plain warning.
rows.rewrite: Kusenokuba nenkungu. Umswakama uyayimema.

rows.en: Your headlights are doing a 'thoughts and prayers'.
rows.reason: 'Iziqhumane' is not the word for headlights (natives use 'izibane zemoto'), and a literal 'iingcinga nemithandazo' does not carry the English idiom.
rows.rewrite: Izibane zemoto yakho azincedi nto — zithandaza nje.

rows.en: The chops are calling. So is the chair.
rows.reason: Concord slip: 'isitulo' is class 7, so 'nayo' is wrong; repeat the verb ('Nesitulo siyabiza').
rows.rewrite: Iitshophu ziyabiza. Nesitulo siyabiza.

rows.en: Even the shade is sweating.
rows.reason: 'Nawumthunzi' is a wrong contraction: na + umthunzi gives 'nomthunzi'; 'uyabila' (sweating) is right.
rows.rewrite: Nditsho nomthunzi uyabila.

rows.en: The sky's reminding us who's boss.
rows.reason: Natural, close to the confirmed 'ukuba ngubani ophambili'; 'inkosi' gives the storm a fitting grandness.

rows.en: Grab your brolly, boet.
rows.reason: Plain and natural; 'isambreli' and 'boet' are both in the confirmed lines, and it reads warm.

rows.en: Nothing a cup of rooibos won't fix.
rows.reason: Missing negative flips the meaning: 'Akukho nto ingalungiswa' says rooibos fixes nothing; it needs 'ingenakulungiswa'.
rows.rewrite: Akukho nto ingenakulungiswa yikomityi ye-rooibos.

rows.en: The fog doesn't care about your schedule.
rows.reason: 'ayikhathalelanga' is correct and gives the fog its attitude; 'ishedyuli' is an accepted loan.

rows.en: The sky is the colour of an old Tupperware lid.
rows.reason: 'isiciko seTupperware esidala' is correct and concrete; the old-lid grey lands as it does in English.

rows.en: The neighbours' pool has never looked so tempting.
rows.draft: Ipuli yommelwane ayikaze ibonakale ihehayo kangaka.
rows.reason: 'yommelwane' is misspelt (umelwane gives 'yomelwane'), and 'ayikaze' reads isiZulu; isiXhosa says 'ayizange'.
rows.rewrite: Ipuli yomelwane ayizange ibonakale ihehayo kangaka.

rows.en: Welkom-cold today. The kind that goes through three jerseys like they aren't there.
rows.draft: Yi-Welkom-cold namhlanje. La makhaza adlula kwii-jersey ezintathu ngathi azikho.
rows.reason: "amakhaza" is the isiZulu word for cold; isiXhosa says ingqele. "Yi-Welkom-cold" and "ii-jersey" are forced code-switches: the natives turned "koue belt" into "ibhanti lengqele", and the app already says ijezi.
rows.rewrite: Ingqele yaseWelkom namhlanje. Idlula kwiijezi ezintathu ngathi azikho.

rows.en: The office aircon war has begun.
rows.reason: Natural and compact. Imfazwe ye-aircon carries the office war exactly, and the code-switch is the one people really use.

rows.en: Sun on your back, freezer on your face.
rows.draft: Ilanga emqolo wakho, i-freezer ebusweni bakho.
rows.reason: "emqolo" is not the locative form: umqolo becomes emqolweni (on your back). The sun-and-freezer contrast lands.
rows.rewrite: Ilanga emqolweni wakho, i-freezer ebusweni bakho.

rows.en: Even your phone's overheating.
rows.reason: "iyashushu" is not how isiXhosa uses -shushu. It is shaped like isiZulu "iyashisa"; a speaker says "ishushu".
rows.rewrite: Nefowuni yakho ishushu kakhulu.

rows.en: Probably fog later. The Boland does this.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi inkungu kamva. I-Boland yenza oku.
rows.reason: "yenza oku" means the Boland is doing this right now. It loses the habit ("the Boland always does this"), and the habit is the joke; "iqhele ukwenza oku" restores it.
rows.rewrite: Mhlawumbi inkungu kamva. IBoland iqhele ukwenza oku.

rows.en: The sun is personally attacking you.
rows.reason: "likuhlasela wena buqu" is natural, and buqu gives the 'personally' sting.

rows.en: Hat, sunnies, sunscreen. Non-negotiable.
rows.reason: "izipeki" has an isiZulu-shaped plural (isiXhosa: iispeki), and plain "ikhrimu" is just cream, not sunscreen. "Akuxoxwa" is stiff; a speaker says "Akukho mpikiswano".
rows.rewrite: Umnqwazi, iispeki zelanga, i-sunscreen. Akukho mpikiswano.

rows.en: The office aircon debate just went to level 5.
rows.draft: Ingxoxo ye-aircon yaseofisini isanda kufikelela inqanaba 5.
rows.reason: "fikelela inqanaba 5" lacks the locative and the numeral concord, and translating "level 5" kills the lockdown echo; people just say ku-level 5. "Ingxoxo" is a calm talk, but this is an argument (impikiswano).
rows.rewrite: Impikiswano ye-aircon e-ofisini isanda kufika ku-level 5.

rows.en: Hold onto your hat! And your kids.
rows.reason: Short and natural. The second beat, Nabantwana bakho, turns just as it does in the English.

rows.en: Garage pie for lunch because the kitchen is lava.
rows.draft: Iphayi yasegaraji ngenxa yokuba ikhitshi yi-lava.
rows.reason: It drops "for lunch". "ngenxa yokuba" is heavy for a quick line (kuba). "ikhitshi yi-lava" is abrupt; a speaker would say the kitchen is as hot as lava.
rows.rewrite: Iphayi yasegaraji yesidlo sasemini, kuba ikhitshi lishushu njenge-lava.

rows.en: Today's plans: exist outside.
rows.reason: "phila ngaphandle" reads as "live outdoors" or "be well outside", not the lazy 'just be outside'.
rows.rewrite: Izicwangciso zanamhlanje: ukuhlala ngaphandle nje.

rows.en: Today's forecast: medium rare.
rows.reason: "medium rare" is kept as the braai term people actually use, which is the right code-switch. The joke depends on knowing the steak term.

rows.en: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.
rows.reason: "ngokwaneleyo kwesuphu" is a calque of 'enough for soup'; a speaker would say "kangangokuba ufuna isuphu".
rows.rewrite: Kubanda kangangokuba ufuna isuphu. Nesuphu yesibini.

rows.en: Clouds today, vibes optional.
rows.reason: It says "the clothes are still safe. Possibly.", a washing-line line about a different idea; there are no clouds and nothing optional.
rows.rewrite: Kunamafu namhlanje. I-vibe ayinyanzelekanga.

rows.en: Your hands are in your pockets and they're not coming out.
rows.reason: Natural everyday phrasing. "aziphumi" carries the stubborn hands well.

rows.en: The kind of day you text someone about.
rows.draft: Uhlobo lwemini othumela umntu umyalezo ngalo.
rows.reason: A correct relative with the you-subject, and the same fragment shape as the confirmed "Uhlobo olwenza..." lines. It reads warm.

rows.en: The hadedas are sleeping. Finally.
rows.reason: "Iintaka" (birds) loses the hadedas, the noisy SA birds the whole joke depends on; sleeping birds at night are no joke.
rows.rewrite: Ii-hadeda zilele. Ekugqibeleni.

rows.en: Hold onto your hat, the Southeaster means business
rows.reason: "iyasebenza" means 'is working', not 'means business'. The natives also render the Southeaster as umoya waseMzantsi-Mpuma; "awudlali" (isn't playing) gives the menace.
rows.rewrite: Bamba umnqwazi wakho, umoya waseMzantsi-Mpuma awudlali.

rows.en: Wet jeans for the rest of the day. The classic punishment.
rows.draft: Ijinsi emanzi yonke imini. Isohlwayo esiqhelekileyo.
rows.reason: It mirrors the confirmed wet-socks line. "Isohlwayo esiqhelekileyo" lands the dry turn.

rows.en: Good enough weather. Not great, not terrible.
rows.reason: "Ayinkulu" means 'it is not big': great taken as size, a wrong word. "eyaneleyo" (sufficient) is stiff for 'good enough'.
rows.rewrite: Imozulu ilungile nje. Ayimnandi kakhulu, kodwa ayimbi.

rows.en: The braai is happening. The braai always happens. We just pull the chairs closer.
rows.draft: I-braai iyenzeka. I-braai ihlala isenzeka. Sitsala nje izitulo sondele.
rows.reason: "Sitsala nje izitulo sondele" has the wrong subject on sondele: it says 'we come closer'. Sisondeza (we bring closer) fixes it.
rows.rewrite: I-braai iyenzeka. I-braai ihlala isenzeka. Sisondeza nje izitulo.

rows.en: Clear-ish night. Don't hold us to the stars.
rows.reason: "obuhle-ish" glues English -ish onto 'beautiful' (clear is obucacileyo), and "Ungasibambi kwiinkwenkwezi" is a literal calque ('don't catch us at the stars') a reader won't follow.
rows.rewrite: Ubusuku obucacileyo kancinci. Ungasibeki ityala ngeenkwenkwezi.

rows.en: SPF 50 or regret it by tonight.
rows.reason: Natural. "uya kuzisola ngokuhlwa" carries 'regret it by tonight' exactly.

rows.en: Forecast: vibes neutral, expectations lower.
rows.reason: "ezingenamfuneko" means 'unnecessary', not neutral. "indlela" means road/way, not expectations, and "indlela eziphantsi" has broken agreement, so the line makes no sense.
rows.rewrite: Isibikezelo: i-vibe iphakathi nendawo. Ungalindeli nto ingako.

rows.en: Probably brewing something. Stay close to a roof.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi kukho into ephekwayo. Hlala kufutshane nophahla.
rows.reason: "kukho into ephekwayo" with no subject can read as food on the stove; make the sky the one cooking so it reads as weather brewing. Second sentence matches the confirmed thunder line.
rows.rewrite: Mhlawumbi isibhakabhaka sipheka into. Hlala kufutshane nophahla.

rows.en: Cancel everything. Even your excuses.
rows.reason: "izizathu" means reasons, not excuses; the app's word for excuses is "izaba" (Akukho zaba), and the joke needs excuses.
rows.rewrite: Rhoxisa yonke into. Nezaba zakho.

rows.en: Schrodinger's rain. It both is and isn't.
rows.reason: "futhi" is isiZulu (isiXhosa says kwaye), and "Iyakho" is not a form: "it is there" is "ikhona". Schrödinger stays as a name.
rows.rewrite: Imvula kaSchrödinger. Ikhona kwaye ayikho.

rows.en: Maluti-frost morning. Lesotho's exporting it for free.
rows.reason: First sentence is English with a Yi- prefix; isiXhosa has its own words (iqabaka for frost, intsasa for morning), as the natives did with posikhadi and iibhloko zomkhenkce. "iyayithumela" has no clear object.
rows.rewrite: Iqabaka laseMaluti ngale ntsasa. ILesotho isithumelela lona mahala.

rows.en: Halfway to a Highveld thunderstorm. Or not.
rows.reason: Says "small clouds, big sun": no Highveld thunderstorm, no "or not" turn, a different forecast from the English.
rows.rewrite: Isaqhwithi saseHighveld sisendleleni. Okanye hayi.

rows.en: The southeaster's arrived. Uninvited, as usual.
rows.draft: Umoya wasemzantsi ufikile. Ungamenyanga, njengoko eqhelile.
rows.reason: "njengoko eqhelile" uses the person concord e- for umoya and is stiff; the everyday phrase is "njengesiqhelo". ("wasemzantsi" is the south wind, close enough to the southeaster.)
rows.rewrite: Umoya wasemzantsi ufikile. Ungamenyanga, njengesiqhelo.

rows.en: Your iced coffee melted before you reached the car.
rows.draft: Ikofu yakho yomkhenkce inyibilikile ngaphambi kokufika emotweni.
rows.reason: "ikofu yomkhenkce" is a literal calque (people say i-iced coffee), and "ngaphambi kokufika" leaves it unclear who reached the car; say "phambi kokuba ufike".
rows.rewrite: I-iced coffee yakho inyibilike phambi kokuba ufike emotweni.

rows.en: The braai is cancelled. Yes, really.
rows.reason: "Ukugrila" is the stiff word the natives replaced with braai in their own ruling; "nyhani" is fine.
rows.rewrite: I-braai irhoxisiwe. Ewe, nyhani.

rows.en: Your future self will thank you for that sunscreen.
rows.draft: Wena wakusasa uya kukubulela ngekhrimu yelanga.
rows.reason: "kusasa" means morning in isiXhosa (tomorrow is isiZulu usage), so "wena wakusasa" reads "you of the morning"; future self is "wena wangomso".
rows.rewrite: Wena wangomso uya kukubulela ngekhrimu yelanga.

rows.en: Cape Doctor is doing rounds today
rows.reason: "UGqirha waseKapa" reads as an actual Cape Town doctor, losing the wind (natives keep I-Cape Doctor as a name), and "wenza iindwendwe" means "makes guests", not doing rounds.
rows.rewrite: I-Cape Doctor ityelela izigulana zayo namhlanje.

rows.en: The braai is the social calendar. Show up.
rows.reason: Literal throughout: "Ukugrila" is the stiff word natives replace with braai, "ikhalenda yentlalo" is a calque, and "Bonakala" means "be visible", not "show up" (a speaker says Fika or Yiza).
rows.rewrite: Yonke into yentlalo yenzeka kwi-braai. Fika.

rows.en: The umbrella broke on the first gust. Classic.
rows.reason: "ngomoya wokuqala" says "by the first wind", not the first gust, and "Okwesiqhelo" is not the everyday "Classic"; the confirmed lines use "Into eqhelekileyo leyo".
rows.rewrite: Isambreli siphuke xa umoya uqala nje ukuvuthuza. Into eqhelekileyo leyo.

rows.en: Good soup weather, not gonna lie.
rows.reason: Plain, natural and warm; drops "not gonna lie", the way the natives kept a line that dropped "give or take".

rows.en: The aircon remote is now public property. Negotiate.
rows.draft: I-aircon remote ngoku yimpahla kawonke-wonke. Xoxa.
rows.reason: "impahla kawonke-wonke" is the natural way to say public property, and "Xoxa" (argue it out) carries the household turn.

rows.en: Days like this is why we put up with the load shedding.
rows.draft: Iimini ezinje zezinto ezisenza sinyamezele i-load shedding.
rows.reason: Natural; "sinyamezele i-load shedding" is how people say it, the same shape as the confirmed "Yiyo le nto sihlala eMzantsi Afrika".

rows.en: The morning forgot to render.
rows.reason: "ukurenda" is a forced loan most readers won't know and sounds like renting; the app's own word for this is "ukulayisha" (Imozulu yanamhlanje: isalayisha).
rows.rewrite: Intsasa ilibele ukulayisha.

rows.en: Your hairstyle? Gone. Accept it.
rows.reason: Natural three beats; "Simkile. Yamkela." matches the confirmed "Yamkela" register and lands dry.

rows.en: The sky's on mute. Nobody's complaining.
rows.reason: "sithule" (gone quiet) is a fair image for mute, and "Akukho mntu ukhalazayo" is everyday isiXhosa.

rows.en: The fridge door is getting a workout today.
rows.reason: "lufumana ukuzilolonga" is a calque of "getting a workout"; a speaker would make the door do it: "luyazilolonga".
rows.rewrite: Ucango lwefriji luyazilolonga namhlanje.

rows.en: The world ends two metres past the gate.
rows.draft: Ihlabathi liphela kwiimitha ezimbini ngaphesheya kwesango.
rows.reason: Clear and natural; "ngaphesheya kwesango" (the far side of the gate) works, and the fog joke lands.

rows.en: This is the weather we brag about overseas.
rows.reason: Natural; "esiziqhayisa ngayo phesheya" carries the national brag exactly.

rows.en: Three hadedas, two crows, one shivering human at the bird feeder.
rows.draft: Ii-hadedas ezintathu, ama-crows amabini, umntu omnye ongcangcazelayo e-bird feeder.
rows.reason: "ama-crows" is the flagged code-switch: isiXhosa says amahlungulu. "Ii-hadedas" doubles the plural (ii-hadeda), and "e-bird feeder" should be "kwi-bird feeder".
rows.rewrite: Ii-hadeda ezintathu, amahlungulu amabini, nomntu omnye ongcangcazelayo kwi-bird feeder.

rows.en: Breezy, probably. Maybe more.
rows.reason: Plain and natural; the doubled "mhlawumbi" mirrors the hedging the natives already let stand.

rows.en: Dark outside, bright tomorrow.
rows.reason: "Mnyama" needs its concord ("Kumnyama"), and "kukhanya ngomso" is present tense; tomorrow needs "kuya kukhanya".
rows.rewrite: Kumnyama ngaphandle, kodwa ngomso kuya kukhanya.

rows.en: Save this one in the memory bank.
rows.reason: Plain, natural 'keep this day in memory'; 'memory bank' is lost but the warm remark reads warm.

rows.en: Big sky energy. Small human response.
rows.draft: Amandla amakhulu esibhakabhaka. Impendulo encinci yomntu.
rows.reason: Word-for-word: 'Impendulo encinci yomntu' (a person's small answer) is not how anyone would say it; the turn is lost and the line reads as two translated fragments.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka sizibonakalisa ngamandla. Thina, sithe cwaka nje.

rows.en: Shorts weather? This is underwear weather.
rows.draft: Imozulu yamabhlukhwe amafutshane? Le yimozulu yamanqisi.
rows.reason: 'amabhlukhwe amafutshane' is misspelt with the wrong concord (natives write iibhulukhwe ezimfutshane / ii-shorts); 'amanqisi' is not an attested word for underwear.
rows.rewrite: Imozulu yee-shorts? Hayi, le yimozulu ye-underwear.

rows.en: Rain so heavy it should pay rent.
rows.reason: 'Imvula enzima' (heavy as in weighty/difficult) is stiff for heavy rain, and the 'so heavy that' link is missing, so the rent joke has no setup.
rows.rewrite: Le mvula ina kakhulu kangangokuba ifanele ihlawule irenti.

rows.en: The ceiling fan is doing its best, but its best is not enough.
rows.draft: Ifeni yophahla yenza okusemandleni ayo, kodwa okusemandleni ayo akwanelanga.
rows.reason: 'Ifeni yophahla' (fan of the roof) is a calque, and the idiom wants 'konke': yenza konke okusemandleni ayo; the repeated phrase is heavy.
rows.rewrite: Ifeni yenza konke okusemandleni ayo, kodwa akwanelanga.

rows.en: Your driveway is a mystery novel right now.
rows.draft: Indlela yakho yokungena yinoveli yemfihlakalo ngoku.
rows.reason: 'Indlela yakho yokungena' reads as 'your way of getting in', not a driveway; people just say i-driveway.
rows.rewrite: I-driveway yakho ngoku ifana nenoveli yemfihlakalo.

rows.en: The sky's having a full-on tantrum.
rows.reason: 'siqumba ngokupheleleyo' (is getting angry completely) is translated-sounding; the tantrum needs the child image to land.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka sinomsindo okomntwana.

rows.en: Hot chocolate is not a want. It's a need.
rows.reason: 'ayikokufuna' (it is not to want) is stiff; the natural frame is the confirmed 'ayisosipho' pattern with isinqwenelo / imfuneko.
rows.rewrite: I-hot chocolate ayisosinqwenelo. Yimfuneko.

rows.en: Even the hadedas sound happy.
rows.reason: Natural, but 'even' is dropped, and that is the joke (the loudest birds sound happy); 'Iintaka zivakala zivuya' is just a plain remark.
rows.rewrite: Nditsho neentaka zivakala zivuya.

rows.en: The bins are on an adventure again.
rows.reason: Urban code-switch the way people talk (like 'siku-ultra mode'); the bins-as-travellers image lands.

rows.en: Stay safe. The sky is making a point.
rows.reason: 'inkcukacha' means a detail, so 'senza inkcukacha' says 'is making a detail', not 'making a point'.
rows.rewrite: Hlala ukhuselekile. Isibhakabhaka sizama ukusixelela into.

rows.en: Lightning's putting Eskom's grid to shame.
rows.reason: 'Umbane' is both lightning and electricity, so the Eskom jab lands even better than the English; 'ubeka ehlazweni' is idiomatic.

rows.en: The lapa cushions are crispy.
rows.reason: 'zi-crispy' forces an English adjective into a verb slot (the reviewer already flagged ii-crispy as awkward); say what the sun did in isiXhosa.
rows.rewrite: Iikhushini ze-lapa zitshiswe lilanga.

rows.en: The dams are doing a happy dance.
rows.reason: 'enza umdaniso ovuyayo' (make a dance that is happy) is a calque; a speaker would have the dams dance with joy.
rows.rewrite: Amadama axhentsa ngovuyo.

rows.en: Somewhere an estate agent is saying 'lifestyle'.
rows.reason: 'Kwezinye iindawo' is 'in some places'; natives write 'kwenye indawo' for somewhere; and 'umthengisi wendlu' is the seller of one house, not an estate agent (wezindlu).
rows.rewrite: Kwenye indawo umthengisi wezindlu uthi 'lifestyle'.

rows.en: Storm's possible. The braai might need a rain check.
rows.draft: Isaqhwithi siyenzeka. Ukugrila kungafuna olunye usuku.
rows.reason: 'siyenzeka' says the storm IS happening, not that it's possible (sisenokwenzeka); 'ukugrila' is the stiff word the natives replaced with braai.
rows.rewrite: Isaqhwithi sisenokwenzeka. I-braai ingafuna olunye usuku.

rows.en: Even the hadedas are quiet.
rows.reason: Natural, but 'even' is gone, and it carries the turn (the noisiest birds have gone silent); add 'Nditsho ne-'.
rows.rewrite: Nditsho neentaka zithe cwaka.

rows.en: The duvet had the right idea this morning.
rows.reason: Reads naturally, 'ngale ntsasa' as in the confirmed lines; the duvet-was-right turn comes through.

rows.en: Outside has betrayed you and you went anyway.
rows.draft: Ngaphandle kukukhaphele kwaye nokuba kunjalo uhambile.
rows.reason: Sentence-initial 'Ngaphandle' reads as 'except/without'; the subject is 'Phandle'; and 'kwaye nokuba kunjalo uhambile' is stiff for 'and you went anyway'.
rows.rewrite: Phandle kukukhaphele, kodwa uphume nangona kunjalo.

rows.en: If you can read this, you're too close.
rows.reason: Clean and natural; the bumper-sticker tailgating joke works the same in isiXhosa.

rows.en: If you're inside, you're doing it wrong.
rows.reason: 'wenza ngokuphosakeleyo' is formal and translated; a speaker would say 'uyaphazama', and 'usengaphakathi' (still inside) sharpens the jab.
rows.rewrite: Ukuba usengaphakathi, uyaphazama.

rows.en: Someone's braai just got ruined.
rows.reason: 'Ukugrila' is the stiff word the natives rejected; everyone says braai.
rows.rewrite: I-braai yomntu isanda konakala.

rows.en: Lekker koud, but the rugby fields are about to look perfect.
rows.draft: Lekker koud, kodwa amabala e-rugby sele eza kujongeka perfect.
rows.reason: 'sele eza kujongeka' (already about to look) clashes, so drop 'sele'; the rest (Lekker koud, amabala e-rugby, perfect) is how people code-switch.
rows.rewrite: Lekker koud, kodwa amabala e-rugby aza kujongeka perfect.

rows.en: The ozone layer called. It's on leave.
rows.reason: 'ifownile' breaks isiXhosa spelling; the loan verb is ukufowuna (cf. confirmed 'Ifowuni'), so it should be 'ifowunile'. 'Iku-leave' is natural.
rows.rewrite: I-ozone layer ifowunile. Iku-leave.

rows.en: The garden is somewhere out there. We trust the process.
rows.reason: Drops 'somewhere' (ndaweni ithile), so the fog joke goes: 'Igadi ikhona ngaphandle' is just a fact; 'Siyithemba inkqubo' is a calque of the English idiom 'trust the process'.
rows.rewrite: Igadi ikhona ngaphandle, ndaweni ithile. Siyakholelwa nje.

rows.en: Cold enough that the milk-bottle-on-the-stoep is now a cooler box.
rows.draft: Kubanda ngokwaneleyo ukuba i-milk-bottle-on-the-stoep ngoku iyi-cooler box.
rows.reason: The English compound 'i-milk-bottle-on-the-stoep' is dropped in whole, which is not how people code-switch; 'Kubanda ngokwaneleyo ukuba' is a calque of 'cold enough that'. A speaker would say 'kangangokuba'.
rows.rewrite: Kubanda kangangokuba ibhotile yobisi phaya kwi-stoep sele iyi-cooler box.

rows.en: Days like this should come with a soundtrack.
rows.reason: Natural, with the code-switched 'ne-soundtrack' the way people say it. The warm remark lands.

rows.en: Visibility sponsored by nobody.
rows.reason: 'kuxhaswe ngubani. Mntu.' reads as 'sponsored by whom? Person.', a question and a stray noun. The 'nobody' (akukho mntu) is lost and the line makes no sense.
rows.rewrite: Ukubonakala kwanamhlanje: akukho mntu ukuxhasayo.

rows.en: Grey skies, low conviction.
rows.reason: 'ukholo' means religious faith, so 'ukholo oluphantsi' reads as 'weak faith', not low forecast certainty. A speaker would say 'ukuqiniseka'.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka esimpunga, ukuqiniseka kuphantsi.

rows.en: This is why Noah built a boat.
rows.draft: Yiyo le nto uNowa wakha umkhombe.
rows.reason: 'Yiyo le nto' plus the Bible's own 'uNowa' and 'umkhombe' (the ark). It is a reference every reader gets.

rows.en: A hoodie and an attitude. That's today.
rows.reason: 'isimilo' for attitude matches the natives' own 'Isimilo siyanyanzelelwa'. 'Namhlanje kunje' is a plain, natural close.

rows.en: The duvet is calling and the duvet is winning.
rows.reason: 'iyabiza' matches the confirmed 'Ama-tong ayabiza', and 'iyaphumelela' is the normal verb for winning. The repetition keeps the two-beat turn.

rows.en: Wait it out indoors. The mountains aren't going anywhere.
rows.reason: 'Yima phakathi' means 'stand in the middle', not 'wait indoors'. Indoors is 'ngaphakathi' (as in 'Hlala ngaphakathi'). The second sentence is fine.
rows.rewrite: Hlala ngaphakathi ude kudlule. Iintaba aziyi ndawo.

rows.en: Perfect excuse to cancel plans.
rows.reason: 'isizathu esihle' is 'a good reason'. 'Perfect' is 'egqibeleleyo' (natives made this exact fix on 'ezilungileyo'), and 'excuse' is 'izaba', which carries the cheek.
rows.rewrite: Izaba ezigqibeleleyo zokurhoxisa izicwangciso.

rows.en: The Cape Doctor is making house calls.
rows.reason: 'UGqirha waseKapa' turns the wind into a literal doctor (natives keep 'I-Cape Doctor'), and 'wenza iindwendwe' means 'makes guests', not house calls. The meaning is lost.
rows.rewrite: I-Cape Doctor ihamba indlu ngendlu namhlanje.

rows.en: Slowly becoming a puddle in the corner.
rows.reason: 'Kancinane' is isiZulu; isiXhosa says 'kancinci (kancinci)'. 'ndiba' should be the subjunctive 'ndibe' after 'ndijika' (cf. confirmed 'ijika ibe').
rows.rewrite: Kancinci kancinci ndijika ndibe lichibana ekoneni.

rows.en: Time to dig out that ugly beanie.
rows.reason: 'ukumba' is literal digging in soil; 'dig out' here is 'ukukhupha'. 'beanie imbi' says 'the beanie is ugly' rather than 'the ugly beanie' ('embi'). 'Ixesha' should be 'Lixesha', as in 'lixesha lejezi'.
rows.rewrite: Lixesha lokukhupha loo beanie yakho embi.

rows.en: Perfect weather for existing without enthusiasm.
rows.reason: 'elungele' is 'suitable', not 'perfect' ('egqibeleleyo'). 'ngaphandle kwentshisekelo' is stiff and bookish; a speaker would say 'ungenamdla'.
rows.rewrite: Imozulu egqibeleleyo yokuphila nje, ungenamdla.

rows.en: The fynbos is loving it. You should too.
rows.reason: 'iyakuthanda' reads as 'it loves you', not 'it's loving it', and 'Nawe kufanele' is left unfinished ('you too should...').
rows.rewrite: Ifynbos iyayonwabela le mozulu. Nawe yonwabele.

rows.en: Cold's the bet. Don't trust a sunny window in winter.
rows.draft: Ukubanda koko sikubhejayo. Ungathembi ifestile enelanga ebusika.
rows.reason: 'Ukubanda koko sikubhejayo' is broken: 'koko' means 'rather/but', not 'is what'. The second sentence is natural and keeps the joke.
rows.rewrite: Sibheja ngokubanda. Ungathembi ifestile enelanga ebusika.

rows.en: Thunder rolling in. Inside is the move.
rows.reason: Both halves are native-confirmed phrasings ('Iindudumo ziyeza', 'Hlala ngaphakathi'). It is plain, so the 'is the move' slang flavour is lost, but it is right.

rows.en: Fog's on the cards. The sky's being coy about it.
rows.reason: 'ikwithuba' is the calque of 'on the cards' that natives replaced with 'isenokwenzeka/isenokubakho'. 'siyazenza' reads as 'is pretending/showing off', not coy.
rows.rewrite: Inkungu isenokubakho. Isibhakabhaka asifuni ukutsho ngqo.

rows.en: Chilly, most likely. Layer up to be safe.
rows.reason: Mirrors the confirmed 'X, mhlawumbi' shape. 'Nxiba iimpahla ezininzi' is plain and correct; the 'to be safe' nuance is lightly dropped.

rows.en: Grey, probably. We've seen it surprise us.
rows.reason: 'Mpunga, mhlawumbi' matches the confirmed 'Mhlawumbi mpunga'. 'Sakha sabona kusothusa' is a natural isiXhosa 'we've seen it surprise us'.

rows.en: Probably cold. Take the jersey, you'll thank us.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi kuyabanda. Thatha ijezi, uya kusibulela.
rows.reason: Everyday isiXhosa throughout ('Thatha ijezi, uya kusibulela'). The warm nudge lands.

rows.en: Visibility: vibes only.
rows.reason: Urban code-switch the way the natives keep 'i-vibe'. It is understood, though the joke is thin.

rows.en: Take a moment. Look up. You're welcome.
rows.reason: Short and natural. 'Wamkelekile' for 'you're welcome' is the natives' own usage ('Imozulu ye-postcard. Wamkelekile.').

rows.en: The fridge feels warmer than the lounge today.
rows.reason: 'iziva' is a calque: the fridge 'feels itself' warm. For how a thing feels to the touch, a speaker says 'ivakala' (as in confirmed 'zivakala njengeebhloko zomkhenkce').
rows.rewrite: Ifriji ivakala ifudumele kunelawunji namhlanje.

rows.en: Probably hot. We'll all find out together.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi kushushu. Siya kufumanisa sonke kunye.
rows.reason: Natural hedge with mhlawumbi plus the shared shrug of 'siya kufumanisa sonke'; 'sonke kunye' is a touch redundant but reads fine.

rows.en: Somewhere a cricket is really giving it.
rows.reason: irhejane is not the word for a cricket (it reads as a rhino), and 'lizimisele ngokwenene' (is really determined) loses the singing, so the line says something else.
rows.rewrite: Kwenye indawo isinambuzane sicula ngamandla aso onke.

rows.en: This is the sky's performance review. It passed.
rows.reason: Agreement: 'Luphumelele' makes the review pass, not the sky (isibhakabhaka needs 'Siphumelele'); 'uhlolo' is stiffer than 'uvavanyo', which the natives use.
rows.rewrite: Olu luvavanyo lwesibhakabhaka. Siphumelele.

rows.en: The dog is staring at the rain like it's a personal insult.
rows.draft: Inja ijonge imvula ngathi yinto yobuqu.
rows.reason: 'ngathi yinto yobuqu' means 'as if it's something personal' - the insult, which is the joke, is gone.
rows.rewrite: Inja ijonge imvula ngathi le mvula iyithukile.

rows.en: Cloud cover with main-character syndrome.
rows.reason: Says 'the sun arrives and comes out' - nothing about cloud or main-character syndrome; different weather, different meaning.
rows.rewrite: Amafu azenza umlinganiswa ophambili namhlanje.

rows.en: This weather has 'meh' written all over it.
rows.draft: Le mozulu ibhalwe 'meh' kuyo yonke indawo.
rows.reason: 'ibhalwe ... kuyo yonke indawo' is a word-for-word calque of 'written all over it'; a speaker would just call the weather 'meh', like the natives' 'I-vibe yi-beige'.
rows.rewrite: Le mozulu yi-'meh' kwaphela.

rows.en: Sky's drafting, not committing.
rows.reason: Natural isiXhosa but a different line: 'carry a shirt and a hoodie - both' is packing advice, not the undecided sky.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka sisaceba nje, asikenzi sigqibo.

rows.en: The fog ate the neighbourhood.
rows.reason: Same engine as the native-kept 'Inkungu iyiselile intaba'; 'itye indawo' is short, natural and keeps the fog-as-eater image.

rows.en: Saturday energy: maximum. Responsibilities: minimum.
rows.reason: Colon structure the natives accept (cf. 'Ukusela amanzi: ewe. Onke.'); concords right, uxanduva/lusezantsi lands the contrast.

rows.en: 50/50 on getting wet. Like a coin toss.
rows.reason: 'ukufumana amanzi' means getting/obtaining water, not getting wet; 'Njengomdlalo' (like a game) loses the coin toss.
rows.rewrite: I-50/50 ukuba uza kuba manzi. Njengokuphosa ingqekembe.

rows.en: Looks settled out there. Roughly.
rows.reason: Plain and natural; mhlawumbi as the dry hedge matches the native-kept 'Siqinisekile mhlawumbi'.

rows.en: At least the garden's happy. Someone has to be.
rows.draft: Ubuncinane igadi iyavuya. Umntu kufuneka avuye.
rows.reason: 'Ubuncinane' is 'at minimum', not the consoling 'at least' (natives use 'Noko'); 'Umntu kufuneka avuye' (a person must be happy) is stiff.
rows.rewrite: Noko igadi yona iyavuya. Kufuneka kubekho ovuyayo.

rows.en: Trust issues with the sky today.
rows.reason: 'Iingxaki zokuthemba' is a calque of 'trust issues'; a speaker would simply say we don't trust the sky.
rows.rewrite: Namhlanje asisithembi tu isibhakabhaka.

rows.en: The kind of sky that makes you grateful for free things.
rows.draft: Uhlobo lwesibhakabhaka olwenza ubulele izinto zasimahla.
rows.reason: Warm and close to the natives' 'Luhlobo lwemini olukwenza...'; one slip: grateful FOR needs 'ngezinto' ('ubulele izinto' is thanking the things), and 'olukwenza' as in the confirmed line.
rows.rewrite: Uhlobo lwesibhakabhaka olukwenza ubulele ngezinto zasimahla.

rows.en: Cloudy-ish. Don't bet the braai on it.
rows.reason: 'Linamafu-ish' glues English -ish onto isiXhosa awkwardly, and 'ukugrila' is the stiff word the natives replaced with braai.
rows.rewrite: Kunamafu kancinci. Sukubheja nge-braai yakho.

rows.en: Table Mountain's tablecloth is out.
rows.reason: 'Ilaphu ... liphumile' is natural (like 'ilanga liphumile'); place name kept as people say it, and the tablecloth image carries for Capetonians.

rows.en: Night looks calm. Models permitting.
rows.draft: Ubusuku bubonakala buzolile. Ukuba iimodeli ziyavuma.
rows.reason: Natural; 'Ukuba iimodeli ziyavuma' is the same relaxed models-hedge as the native-kept low-confidence lines.

rows.en: Solidarity to everyone with one wet shoe right now.
rows.draft: Imanyano kubo bonke abanesihlangu esinye esimanzi ngoku.
rows.reason: 'Imanyano kubo bonke' is a calque - imanyano reads as unity/union; a speaker would say 'we are with' everyone. The wet-shoe part is good.
rows.rewrite: Sikunye nabo bonke abanesihlangu esinye esimanzi ngoku.

rows.en: Bring a jacket. Or don't. We're only fairly sure.
rows.draft: Thatha ibhatyi. Okanye hayi. Siqinisekile nje mhlawumbi.
rows.reason: Mirrors the native-kept 'Okanye ungaphakishi. Asazi nathi.' and 'Siqinisekile mhlawumbi'; the shrug lands.

rows.en: The clouds are having a moment.
rows.reason: 'anethuba lawo' means 'have their chance/turn', which loses the dramatic, emotional sense of 'having a moment'.
rows.rewrite: Amafu anomvakalelo namhlanje.

rows.en: Stay hydrated or become a biltong.
rows.reason: 'Hlala unamanzi' (stay with water) is a stiff calque of 'stay hydrated'; a speaker says drink water. 'yi-biltong' code-switch is right.
rows.rewrite: Sela amanzi, kungenjalo uza kuba yi-biltong.

rows.en: Could get gusty. The forecast's a bit loose on this one.
rows.draft: Kunokuba nomoya. Uqikelelo luxega kule nto.
rows.reason: 'Uqikelelo luxega kule nto' is a word-for-word 'loose on this one'; natives say isibikezelo for the forecast and 'asiqinisekanga' for unsure. 'Gusty' wants umoya onamandla.
rows.rewrite: Kunokubakho umoya onamandla. Isibikezelo asiqinisekanga kangako ngale nto.

rows.en: The traffic just remembered rain exists. Again.
rows.draft: Itrafikhi isanda kukhumbula ukuba imvula ikhona. Kwakhona.
rows.reason: Line works; spelling slip 'Itrafikhi' - the natives write 'Ithrafiki'.
rows.rewrite: Ithrafiki isand' ukukhumbula ukuba imvula ikhona. Kwakhona.

rows.en: Cape Town just got a dimmer switch.
rows.reason: 'ukuncipha' is intransitive (to get less); a switch that reduces light needs 'ukunciphisa'.
rows.rewrite: IKapa lisand' ukufumana iswitshi yokunciphisa ukukhanya.

rows.en: Cloud's the call. With an asterisk.
rows.reason: 'Amafu lulo uluvo' is a clumsy copula ('the clouds, it is the opinion'), and 'Kunophawu' means 'there is a mark/sign': the caveat the asterisk carries is lost, so the reader gets no forecast-with-a-catch.
rows.rewrite: Sithi ngamafu namhlanje. Kodwa asiqinisekanga ngokupheleleyo.

rows.en: The garden's saying dankie at last.
rows.reason: Natural and warm; 'enkosi' carries the dankie, and 'ithi ekugqibeleni enkosi' reads like speech.

rows.en: The sky's undecided. So are we.
rows.reason: 'asikagqibi' reads as 'hasn't finished yet', not 'undecided'; the natives say 'ukwenza isigqibo'. Bare 'Nathi.' is thin; 'Nathi kunjalo' lands the turn.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka asikenzi sigqibo. Nathi kunjalo.

rows.en: The frogs have entered the chat.
rows.reason: 'inkcazo' means explanation/description, not chat, so the frogs 'entered the explanation'; urban speakers just say 'kwi-chat'.
rows.rewrite: Amasele angene kwi-chat.

rows.en: The couch has made a compelling case for staying.
rows.reason: 'icala elinamandla' is 'a strong side', a calque of 'compelling case' that does not read as an argument; a speaker would say the couch gave you a good reason.
rows.rewrite: Isofa ikunike isizathu esivakalayo sokuba uhlale ekhaya.

rows.en: Layers off by 11. Layers on by 4. Highveld classic.
rows.draft: Ii-layers off ngo-11. Ii-layers on ngo-4. Highveld classic.
rows.reason: English with a prefix stuck on: 'off', 'on', 'classic' have no isiXhosa verb or structure; the natives replace loans like this with isiXhosa words.
rows.rewrite: Ukhulula iijezi ngo-11. Uphinda uzinxiba ngo-4. Yi-Highveld leyo.

rows.en: Jislaaik, it's properly hot!
rows.reason: 'ngempela' is isiZulu; isiXhosa says 'ngenene'. 'Yhuu' is right, as in the kept storm line.
rows.rewrite: Yhuu, kushushu ngenene!

rows.en: Not a hairstyle in sight. Just survivors.
rows.draft: Akukho simbo seenwele esibonwayo. Abasindileyo kuphela.
rows.reason: Plain and natural ('esibonwayo' follows the confirmed 'Akukho nto ibonwayo'); the survivors turn comes through.

rows.en: You're not cold, you're 'lekker koud'. Big difference.
rows.reason: 'Akubandi' is 'it is not cold', not 'you're not cold' (Awubandi); bare 'u-' before the slang reads like a name. 'Umahluko mkhulu' is the spoken predicate.
rows.rewrite: Awubandi, uku-'lekker koud'. Umahluko mkhulu.

rows.en: Your high beams are making it worse, boet.
rows.draft: Ii-high beam zakho zenza kube kubi, boet.
rows.reason: 'zenza kube kubi' is 'make it bad'; the comparative 'worse' needs 'ngakumbi'. Otherwise natural.
rows.rewrite: Ii-high beam zakho zenza kube kubi ngakumbi, boet.

rows.en: Thunder so close the walls shook. Respect.
rows.reason: No 'so ... that' link (kangangokuba), so it reads 'thunder that is near the walls shook'; 'zachachamba' is not a word I can confirm (plain: zashukuma); 'Intlonipho.' as a bare noun reads like a heading.
rows.rewrite: Iindudumo bezikufutshane kangangokuba iindonga zashukuma. Siyazihlonipha.

rows.en: This is the day the brochure was talking about.
rows.reason: Grammar holds, but 'incwadana' is just 'booklet', so the tourism promise is lost; the confirmed line uses 'ibrochure yezokhenketho'.
rows.rewrite: Le yimini ibrochure yezokhenketho eyayithetha ngayo.

rows.en: Even the shade is warm. Good luck out there.
rows.reason: 'Inyhani enhle' is 'a nice truth', not good luck; good luck is 'ithamsanqa'. First sentence is fine.
rows.rewrite: Kwanomthunzi ufudumele. Ube nethamsanqa phaya phandle.

rows.en: The sun sent an out-of-office reply.
rows.reason: Natural code-switch ('i-out-of-office', as in the confirmed weekend line); the sun-as-worker joke lands.

rows.en: Everyone's forgotten how to drive. Again.
rows.reason: Natives change bare 'Bonke' to 'Wonke umntu' (see the pool line); 'balibele ukuqhuba' can read 'forgot to drive' rather than 'forgot how'.
rows.rewrite: Wonke umntu ulibele indlela yokuqhuba. Kwakhona.

rows.en: The pavement is a river and the river has plans.
rows.reason: Two beats with a turn, natural; 'unezicwangciso' mirrors the confirmed 'Isibhakabhaka sinezicwangciso'.

rows.en: You could fry an egg on the N1.
rows.reason: 'ukubhaka' is to bake; frying an egg is 'ukuqhotsa'.
rows.rewrite: Ungaqhotsa iqanda kwi-N1.

rows.en: The shade is working harder than you today.
rows.reason: Natural comparative ('kunawe') in the same shape as the confirmed kettle line; the shade gets agency.

rows.en: Every taxi on the road has decided to freestyle.
rows.draft: Yonke itekisi endleleni ikhethe ukudlala ngokukhululekileyo.
rows.reason: 'ukudlala ngokukhululekileyo' is 'to play freely', a calque that loses the driving sense; 'itekisi' is usually 'iteksi'; people keep 'freestyle' as the loan.
rows.rewrite: Zonke iiteksi endleleni zigqibe kwelokuba zenze i-freestyle.

rows.en: The tar is soft. The people are softer.
rows.reason: The turn is lost: 'Abantu bathambile' says people are soft, not softer; needs 'ngakumbi', and 'bona' sets up the contrast.
rows.rewrite: I-tar ithambile. Abantu bona bathambe ngakumbi.

rows.en: Watch for fog — it likes to arrive unannounced.
rows.draft: Lumkela inkungu — ithanda ukufika ingazange yazise.
rows.reason: 'ingazange yazise' is 'it never announced', not 'without announcing'; a speaker says 'ingaxelanga'.
rows.rewrite: Lumkela inkungu — ithanda ukufika ingaxelanga.

rows.en: The weekend doesn't get better than this.
rows.reason: Natural, with 'bhetele' as in the confirmed lines; reads warm.

rows.en: Your washing just moved to the neighbour's yard.
rows.draft: Impahla yakho isanda kukhutshelwa kwiyadhi yommelwane.
rows.reason: 'isanda kukhutshelwa' is a stiff passive ('was taken out to'), so the washing loses its agency; 'ukufudukela' (to move house to) gives the joke, and 'eyadini' is the usual form.
rows.rewrite: Impahla yakho isand' ukufudukela eyadini yommelwane.

rows.en: Probably clear. Your window's the final say.
rows.draft: Mhlawumbi sicacile isibhakabhaka. Ifestile yakho inegunya lokugqibela.
rows.reason: Carries the hedge and hands the call to the window; 'igunya lokugqibela' is a little formal but natural.

rows.en: Bottle this one. Open it in winter.
rows.reason: The 'le' at the end reads as 'in this bottle' (ebhotileni le), not 'this one (day)'; name the day up front so 'it' has something to point at.
rows.rewrite: Le mini yifake ebhotileni. Uyivule ebusika.

rows.en: The sky's giving mixed signals again.
rows.reason: 'imiqondiso exubileyo' is a word-for-word calque of 'mixed signals' (and 'siphinda sinika' wants the subjunctive 'sinike'); a speaker would just say the sky is confusing us again.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka siyasidida kwakhona.

rows.en: Not the time for hero moves, hey.
rows.reason: 'lamagorha' means 'of heroes' (not the time of heroes), losing the jab at showing off; 'ukuzenza igorha' (acting the hero) carries 'hero moves'.
rows.rewrite: Asilo xesha lokuzenza igorha, hey.

rows.en: This weather needs a life coach.
rows.reason: Plain, correct, and the weather-as-a-person joke comes through; 'umqeqeshi wobomi' is transparent.

rows.en: Feels like the country is on its best behaviour.
rows.reason: 'likwisimo esihle' says the country is in a good state/condition, not behaving well, and 'isimo' leans isiZulu; 'liziphethe kakuhle' is 'behaving itself'.
rows.rewrite: Kuvakala ngathi ilizwe lonke liziphethe kakuhle namhlanje.

rows.en: Your excuse to stay inside just expired.
rows.draft: Isizathu sakho sokuhlala ngaphakathi sisanda kuphelelwa.
rows.reason: 'sisanda kuphelelwa' is left hanging (run out of what?); expired is 'kuphelelwa lixesha', and an excuse is 'izaba' (as in 'Akukho zaba'), 'isizathu' is a reason.
rows.rewrite: Izaba zakho zokuhlala ngaphakathi zisanda kuphelelwa lixesha.

rows.en: Hair plans: cancelled.
rows.reason: The mock-official notice works; 'izicwangciso' and 'zirhoxisiwe' are the right words for plans cancelled.

rows.en: Nobody told the forecast. It just arrived.
rows.draft: Akukho mntu uxelele isibikezelo. Sivele safika.
rows.reason: 'Sivele safika' agrees with isibikezelo, so it says the forecast just arrived; the thing that arrived is the rain (imvula, 'ivele yafika').
rows.rewrite: Akukho mntu uxelele isibikezelo. Imvula ivele yafika nje.

rows.en: The duvet understood the assignment.
rows.reason: Natural, and the duvet knowing its job reads warm, though the 'assignment' meme flattens to 'understood what was needed'.

rows.en: Rooibos consumption just doubled.
rows.reason: 'Ukusetyenziswa' (usage) is bureaucratic for drinking tea, and 'kuphindaphindeka' means repeated over and over, not doubled ('kuphindeka kabini').
rows.rewrite: Ukusela i-rooibos kusanda kuphindeka kabini.

rows.en: Sky's doing the most, but only a little.
rows.reason: Says 'the sun comes out and clears again' (with the doubtful 'licaceke'), nothing of the sky doing the most but only a little; the joke is gone.
rows.rewrite: Isibhakabhaka siyazibonakalisa, kodwa kancinci nje.

rows.en: Three pairs of socks and still not enough.
rows.reason: 'amapheya' reads isiZulu (isiXhosa says 'iiperi'), and 'still' is dropped; 'nangoku' brings back 'and still not enough'.
rows.rewrite: Iiperi ezintathu zeekawusi, kodwa azanelanga nangoku.

rows.en: The sun doesn't care about your plans.
rows.reason: Clean personification: the sun indifferent to your plans; 'alikhathalelanga' carries 'doesn't care about'.

rows.en: Some cloud, some sun. The ratio's anyone's guess.
rows.draft: Amafu akho, ilanga likho. Umlinganiselo ukuqashelo.
rows.reason: 'Umlinganiselo ukuqashelo' is not understandable: 'ukuqashelo' is not a word and there is no copula; 'anyone's guess' is 'akukho mntu waziyo'.
rows.rewrite: Amafu kancinci, ilanga kancinci. Ngubani ophambili? Akukho mntu waziyo.

rows.en: This is the weather the weekend was invented for.
rows.reason: The relative clause 'impelaveki eyenzelwe yona' is tangled and reads translated; a speaker would say the weekend was made for this weather.
rows.rewrite: Impelaveki yenzelwe le mozulu kanye.

rows.en: The sun's on airplane mode.
rows.reason: Natural code-switch, same pattern as the confirmed 'siku-ultra mode'; the sun gone offline lands.

rows.en: Weekend vibes so strong they need their own playlist.
rows.draft: Weekend vibes ezinamandla kakhulu zifuna i-playlist yazo.
rows.reason: Bare English 'Weekend vibes' with no prefix sits outside the sentence, and 'so strong they need' needs 'kangangokuba'.
rows.rewrite: I-vibe yempelaveki inamandla kangangokuba ifuna i-playlist yayo.

rows.en: Grey vibes. The sky matched my Monday.
rows.draft: I-grey vibes. Isibhakabhaka sifana noMvulo wam.
rows.reason: 'I-grey vibes' follows the confirmed 'I-Silent Hill vibes'; 'sifana noMvulo wam' is natural and the turn lands.

rows.en: The owls are judging your screen time.
rows.reason: 'umsebenzi wakho wesikrini' means 'your screen work', not screen time; people just say 'i-screen time'.
rows.rewrite: Izikhova ziyayigweba i-screen time yakho.

rows.en: The braai cover is in the next suburb.
rows.reason: 'isifunda' is a region/district, not a suburb; 'sise-kwi-' reads as 'still in'; 'isigqubuthelo' is stiff where people say 'i-cover'.
rows.rewrite: I-cover yebraai ngoku ikwindawo elandelayo.

rows.en: Perfect night to actually see the Milky Way.
rows.reason: 'iNdlela yaseSisi' is not the isiXhosa name for the Milky Way (it is uMnyele), so a reader will not know what to look for; 'actually' is dropped too.
rows.rewrite: Ubusuku obugqibeleleyo bokubona uMnyele ngokwenene.

rows.en: Almost a braai day.
rows.reason: Says 'clouds will come and go', not 'almost a braai day', and 'azofika' is an isiZulu contraction.
rows.rewrite: Phantse lusuku lwe-braai.

rows.en: Ponytail holders are doing overtime.
rows.reason: 'ngokungaphezulu' (excessively) is vague and stiff for overtime; the confirmed lines say 'iiyure ezongezelelweyo'.
rows.rewrite: Izibopho zeenwele zisebenza iiyure ezongezelelweyo namhlanje.

rows.en: Somewhere a weather reporter is living their best life.
rows.draft: Ndaweni ithile umxeli wemozulu uphila ubomi obuhle.
rows.reason: 'umxeli' is not the usual word for reporter (intatheli), and 'uphila ubomi obuhle' (living a good life) loses 'best life'; say the reporter is thrilled today.
rows.rewrite: Kwenye indawo, intatheli yemozulu yonwabe kakhulu namhlanje.
